title: Dehomogenization of a finite graded module is finite
statement: Let $C=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}C_n$ be a commutative nonnegatively graded ring that is a finite type $C_0$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $M=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}M_n$ be a graded $C$-module, meaning a $C$-module with a direct-sum decomposition into additive subgroups satisfying $C_aM_b\subseteq M_{a+b}$. Assume that $M$ is finitely generated as a $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For a homogeneous $f\in C_d$ with $d>0$, let $C_{(f),0}$ be the degree-zero homogeneous localization [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and let $M_{(f),0}$ be the module of degree-zero fractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]: elements $m/f^k$ with $k\geq0$ and $m\in M_{kd}$, modulo the ordinary module-localization equivalence relation, with scalar multiplication $(c/f^a)(m/f^b)=cm/f^{a+b}$. Then $M_{(f),0}$ is a finitely generated $C_{(f),0}$-module. Neither $C_0$ being Noetherian nor $C$ being generated in degree one is assumed.
